title: Stuck in the Elevator
synopsis: Floor 23. The lights flicker. Three strangers. The fire alarm just went off.

nodes.text: The car jerks and stills. The display says 23. The smell is wrong.

choices.consequence: “Hit the call button” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Tactical.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Brave.

nodes.text: A nurse, a teenager, a man with a briefcase. Each takes you in.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Lead.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Wise.

nodes.text: Two have no signal. The nurse's does.

choices.consequence: “Coordinate” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Smart.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Honest—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: A thin line of smoke under the door. The boy starts coughing.

choices.consequence: “Wet your shirts” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Smart.
You commit to “Lift the ceiling panel.” The story records the instinct as “Brave” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Above the panel, an old maintenance ladder runs to the roof.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Care—follows you into whatever comes next.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Pragmatic.

nodes.text: Roof. Helicopters far off. The nurse hugs you in a way that is years of hugging compressed.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Hug back” back. Honor shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
There is no taking “Help the others up first” back. Honor shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Everyone gets out. The man in the suit, weeping in his SUV, tells you it was his first day.
You stay friends with the nurse. You get drinks every February 4th.
